standard_prerequisites.name: Nilradical as intersection of minimal primes; annihilator and support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Algebra (prime ideals, radicals, and annihilators in Noetherian rings)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the facts that intersection of minimal primes is the nilradical and that a prime avoids the annihilator I exactly when it lies over it.

core_obligations: Write a_1 = a_2 + x and prove x is nilpotent: x maps to zero in the product of the A_p, the intersection of the minimal primes is the nilradical of (0), and the annihilator I of x contains a power of m because no minimal prime of A lies over I (proof lines 7591-7595).

Fix k with x^k = 0 and n with m^n contained in I; expand (a_2 + x)^(k+n) by the binomial theorem and observe every term containing x^i for 1 <= i < k carries a factor a_2^(k+n-i) lying in m, while terms with i >= k vanish; hence a_1^(k+n) = a_2^(k+n) (proof lines 7596-7602).
proof_roadmap: Decompose a_1 = a_2 + x and observe x maps to zero in every minimal-prime localization.
Use reducedness-style radical computation to show x is nilpotent with annihilator containing a power of the maximal ideal.
Expand (a_2 + x) to a large power and use the maximal-ideal condition to kill every mixed term.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a_1, a_2 in the maximal ideal of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring A with equal images in the product of the A_p over minimal primes p satisfy a_1^n = a_2^n for some n. The proof writes a_1 = a_2 + x, proves x is nilpotent because the intersection of the minimal primes is the nilradical and the annihilator of x contains a power of m, and then expands (a_2 + x)^(k+n) by the binomial theorem, with every cross term killed either by a power of x or by a high power of a_2 in m (proof lines 7591-7602). H2: combining nilpotency of x with the binomial expansion under the maximal-ideal hypothesis is the non-routine step.
